record.question:
A company uses a versioned S3 general purpose bucket and wants its application to upload and retrieve new object versions with server-side encryption using customer-provided keys (SSE-C). The bucket is already configured to allow SSE-C writes, and the company will retain a secure mapping of object versions to keys.

Which implementation requirements apply? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use the secure WebSocket protocol to send the encryption key to Amazon S3 before uploading an object.
Set x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key-MD5 to AES256 to select the encryption algorithm.
Include the SSE-C algorithm header set to AES256, the base64-encoded 256-bit key, and the base64-encoded MD5 digest of that key in the applicable upload and retrieval requests.
Upload and retrieve SSE-C objects only through the Amazon S3 console so that the console can retain the encryption keys.
Use HTTPS for SSE-C requests. When using a presigned URL, include the required SSE-C headers in the signed request and supply the matching headers when making the request.

explanation.text:
<<3>> supplies the three SSE-C header values: the algorithm, the key, and a digest that checks key transmission integrity. <<5>> provides the required HTTPS transport and the headers needed when invoking a presigned request. A bare presigned URL in a browser is insufficient for SSE-C.

<<1>> substitutes WebSockets for the S3 HTTPS API. <<2>> confuses the algorithm field with the key-MD5 field. <<4>> is incorrect because the S3 console does not support SSE-C operations and S3 does not retain the supplied encryption key.

Keep each version’s key independently recoverable; losing it makes that version unreadable. Enabling SSE-C does not convert older SSE-S3 versions. Also distinguish permission to use SSE-C from a bucket default: affected new and existing buckets block SSE-C writes by default from April 2026, and applications must explicitly unblock them when required.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ServerSideEncryptionCustomerKeys.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/specifying-s3-c-encryption.html

diagram_alt: A field-role comparison distinguishes the encryption algorithm, secret key, integrity digest and HTTPS transport.

sources.supports: HTTPS, key custody, version mapping, console limitation and April 2026 SSE-C blocking defaults.
Required header roles and presigned URL usage.

editorial_notes: Retained current SSE-C default-blocking caveat and made unblocking a completed prerequisite.
Constrained scope to new versions so enabling SSE-C is not mistaken for re-encrypting historical versions.
